subject: Clarify: non-training commitment scope and provenance evidence
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Sara Lopez <sara.lopez@hiperhealth.com>; legal@hiperhealth.com
Cc: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Feb 2026 10:12:00 -0800
Subject: Clarify: non-training commitment scope and provenance evidence

Hi Sara / Hiper legal team,

Thanks for the productive call earlier. We want to make sure the DPA language and the operational evidence you need line up so procurement can finish the review. A few concrete asks from our side to confirm the scope of the requested "no-training / no-model-improvement" commitment and the evidence you expect: 

- Confirmation that "no-training" covers both (a) retraining the base weights and (b) inclusion of prompt/response pairs in any persistent long-term training store (this excludes ephemeral caching used for session continuity).
- Do you expect a technical proof (e.g., audit logs, model-variant mapping, configuration snapshot) for every production request, or is a representative evidence pack (sample logs + config + architecture diagram) sufficient?
- We need to align on ownership: you indicated HiperHealth requires that prompts+responses remain tenant-owned and not used for model improvement. Do you also require any license assignment for derived outputs (summaries, rewrites) or just assurance that they will not be used to improve models?
- If onshore residency is required for the no-train workload, please confirm preferred region (us-east-1, us-west-2).

I've attached our redlined DPA (Hiper_DPA_redline_v3.pdf) with proposed language edits that map to the operational controls we can provide. Olga has sketched a short dataflow diagram and suggested evidence items. Can you confirm which items are must-haves versus nice-to-have so we can prioritize?

Next steps we propose:
1) Hiper confirms required evidence and residency.
2) Redwood provides an evidence pack (config, sampling logs, model-variant mapping, audit sequence).
3) Legal teams finalize the DPA redline + DocuSign.

Thanks — appreciate the rapid turnaround here.

— Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0193

From: Sara Lopez <sara.lopez@hiperhealth.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: legal@hiperhealth.com
Date: Tue, 3 Feb 2026 13:08:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Clarify: non-training commitment scope and provenance evidence

Thanks Marcus — quick answers below and a couple follow-ups.

- "No-training" needs to include both (a) no weight updates using our data and (b) no inclusion in any long-term training store that could influence future models. Ephemeral cache for session continuity is fine if explicitly time-bounded and not persisted to training storage.
- Representative evidence pack is acceptable to start (we don't need a per-request proof), but it must include configuration snapshots and a reproducible method for mapping production request IDs to any logs we provide.
- Ownership: HiperHealth wants tenant ownership of prompts/responses and exclusive rights to derivative outputs. We are not asking for assignment of Redwood IP in the underlying models, but want contractual assurance that derivatives generated from our data are exclusive to us for the term.
- Residency: prefer us-east-1; can accept us-west-2 as fallback.

Also: our security team will want an explanation of how you segregate telemetry from the no-train tenant to prevent inadvertent bleed into general model metrics. If you can include a brief tech note, that will speed sign-off.

I'll have our legal associate loop in redlines to your attachment by EOD tomorrow.

— Sara Lopez
CTO, HiperHealth
sara.lopez@hiperhealth.com

From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
To: Sara Lopez <sara.lopez@hiperhealth.com>; Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Feb 2026 09:37:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Clarify: non-training commitment scope and provenance evidence

Hi Sara — thanks for the clear replies. Below is a concise technical description of how Redwood would enforce a no-training/no-improvement tenancy and the types of artifacts we can produce as evidence. I'm summarizing at a level your security team can hand to operations.

Operational enforcement (high level):
- Tenant-isolated model variant: we spin up a model variant for HiperHealth that is configured with training disabled. That variant uses the same base model family but is flagged in orchestration as "no_improvement=true" so training pipelines ignore telemetry from it.
- Ephemeral KV cache only: session continuity uses an in-memory KV cache that is garbage-collected after X minutes (configurable); nothing is flushed to the long-term training store.
- Telemetry segregation: request telemetry (latency, token counts) is forked—redacted telemetry sent to general metrics, full request/response detail retained only in the tenant data store when permitted. Access controls and KMS-scoped keys govern retrieval.
- Onshore processing: we can pin instances and storage to us-east-1 for the HiperHealth tenant.

Evidence items we can provide (representative pack):
- Configuration snapshot: orchestration flags, model-variant id, region binding.
- Dataflow diagram: how requests move through runtime (see attached dataflow-diagram.png).
- Sampling logs: a time-bounded sample of request IDs with SHA256 of prompt payloads and a mapping table (request ID -> shard -> variant).
- Audit log extract: sequence of actions showing training pipelines reading/writing model artifacts (to demonstrate the HiperHealth variant was not included).
- Hash-based provenance: hashed identifiers that prove the same request ids generated the responses you received (without revealing raw user content in public channels).

We cannot provide raw production payloads outside of an agreed channel, but we can deliver hashed/sampled proofs and a signed statement from our platform operations that the variant flagged as no_improvement was not fed into training between dates X and Y.

If that meets your bar, Marcus and I can assemble the representative pack and share a temporary secure SFTP for you to pull the artifacts. Neha — can you advise on whether the signed operations attestation should be a PDF or a GPG-signed statement?

— Olga
Olga Petrov
Product Security Lead | Redwood Inference

Perfect — thanks everyone for the quick alignment. Confirming next steps:

1) Redwood will prepare the representative evidence pack (config snapshot, sample logs with hashed payloads, audit extract, signed operations attestation). Expect delivery to a temporary SFTP in us-east-1 by EOD Friday.
2) Legal: we'll incorporate Sara's requested derivative-rights language into the DPA redline and circulate for final comment. If Hiper signs as-is, we will send a DocuSign link (https://docusign.com/hiper-dpa-signature-link) and get the HubSpot deal updated (https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1337/deal/8472).
3) Neha, please prepare the attestation as a PDF and include the orchestration snapshot (variant id + timestamp).

Sara — can you confirm that representative evidence and a signed operations attestation are sufficient for your security/compliance sign-off? If so, we'll mark the procurement checklist as ready and begin the DocuSign flow.

Thanks—
Marcus
